title: "Dual Support Vector Machine"
description: "Original mathematical explanation and worked example informed by MML §12.3."
---

**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), Chapter 12 §12.3. All examples are newly authored.

## Motivation

The SVM can be solved through Lagrange multipliers. In the dual representation, the final weight vector is a combination of training observations, and only certain observations carry nonzero multipliers.

## Derivation and notation

$$
\max_{\alpha_i\geq0}\sum_i\alpha_i-\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_jy_iy_j\boldsymbol x_i^\top\boldsymbol x_j,\quad\sum_i\alpha_iy_i=0
$$

Read this model together with the distributional, geometric or optimisation assumptions. An equation without its domain of validity is not a complete explanation.

## Apply it to our running example

A training observation far from the separating boundary often receives zero alpha; those on or within the margin can become support vectors. In our toy dataset, examples near distances three and four determine the closest separation and matter more than distant points.

## Constraints and interpretation

The formula is the hard-margin linear SVM dual; the soft-margin dual also enforces 0≤alpha_i≤C. Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions connect the primal and dual optima under the appropriate convex assumptions.
